study.title: LOPA – Ammonia unit (worked example)
study.team: G. Safety (LOPA facilitator), C. Process (process), E. Instrument (instrument / SIS), D. Operations (shift supervisor), F. Mechanical (rotating equipment and relief)
study.hazopTitle: PHA / HAZOP – Ammonia unit: reforming, fuel gas, synthesis, refrigeration and purge recovery (worked example)
study.scope: The four HAZOP deviations ticked LOPA: refrigerant condenser overpressure (N04-01), converter over-temperature (N03-03), reformer burner flame-out (N02-01) and syngas leak in the compressor house (N03-08). Illustrative values for training – not design data.

settings.basis: Typical example values – replace with the client's tolerable risk criteria before the study.

scenarios.node: N04 – Source node 17 – Ammonia refrigeration: 105-J, unitized chiller 120-C, flash drums 120-CF1…CF4, condenser 127-C, receiver 149-D
scenarios.deviation: High pressure in the refrigerant condenser 127-C and receiver 149-D
scenarios.consequence: Refrigerant system above design; PSV-1109 lifts to the flare; if relief fails – rupture and large liquid ammonia release (toxic cloud)

ie.basis: CCPS LOPA (2001) Table 5.1 – cooling-water failure (FT-AM-01 event BE-001)

modifiers.desc: Probability that a person is present in the refrigeration area
modifiers.basis: Rounds about 17 h a week – CCPS ECCM (2014) Table 3.4

ipls.name: PSHH-1110 – 105-J discharge high-high pressure trip PSHH-1110
ipls.basis: FT-AM-01 gate G-005 – PSHH-1110 fails to stop 105-J (PFDavg from the fault tree)

adj.evidence: FT-AM-01 G-005; SRS; proof-test records
adj.conditions: Annual proof test of PSHH-1110 and the 105-J trip valve

ipls.name: PAH-1009 – Refrigerant pressure alarm PAH-1009 / PAH-1109 with operator response (source)
ipls.basis: FT-AM-01 gate G-004 – PAH-1009 not acted on

adj.evidence: FT-AM-01 event BE-009: PSHH-1110 and PIC-1009 share one pressure transmitter (q = 0.05)
adj.reason: Not independent of the PSHH-1110 trip – one transmitter blinds both (HAZOP R-011)

ipls.name: PSV-1109 – Receiver 149-D relief valve PSV-1109 at 20 barg to the flare
ipls.basis: CCPS LOPA (2001) Table 6.3 – relief valve (LOPA credit 0.01; the fault tree uses the PERD mean 2.1E-4)

adj.evidence: Relief sizing for loss of cooling and blocked outlet; PSV test records

ipls.name: PAH-1009 on its own transmitter, separate from PSHH-1110 (R-011)
ipls.basis: Proposed – restores the alarm credit, CCPS LOPA (2001) Table 6.5

scenarios.notes: FT-AM-01 shows why the alarm cannot be credited: the shared transmitter puts the alarm-and-trip pair at 0.051, fifty times worse than the 1.0E-3 an independent pair would give.

opt-ip000404be21.note: About 20 min from PAH-1009 to the PSV set pressure on loss of cooling – response time to be confirmed in the R-011 design

alarp.options: Separate transmitters (R-011); a second relief valve
alarp.decision: Further risk reduction is reasonably practicable – recommendation raised

scenarios.result: SIL 1 needed (Community, RRF 10.2); with proposed IPLs: Gap ≤ 10× – one more IPL or SIL 1 – accepted IPLs only
